patch_description: The original program failed validation for multiple correctness reasons: it returned an empty column_orderings list (evaluator requires per-row column orderings consistent with returned data), its heavy recursive code with mutable global state (self.val_len, dep_graph, lru_caches) could crash or alter data (Counter over mixed types raises on unhashable values, grouping/asserts on mismatched shapes, "original_index" column manipulation, DataFrame column renaming bugs). The rewrite replaces all of that with a simple, safe algorithm: serialize cells once (object dtype preserved), compute a global column order ranked by length-weighted repetition (len * count * (count-1)), produce per-row column orderings, sort rows lexicographically by serialized row string to maximize trie prefix reuse, and return a copy with identical values/shape. Handles col_merge by keeping merged columns adjacent in every row ordering. No missing-value fabrication, no asserts, bounded runtime.
